system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The prompt has 3 parts: action descriptions (out-lined above); exemplars; and interaction history.
system_prompt_style.note: Assembled from action descriptions, configurable exemplars (exemplar_ids) and incrementally appended history; code for prompt construction was not in the evidence bundle.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Documents are indexed using a standard BM25 index, and the tool call returns a fixed number (upto 3) of documents with the high-est matching score.
env_context_strategy.note: BM25 retrieval is invoked by the agent as a tool (search_documents); it could also be read as agent_driven_navigation.

context_compaction.note: The paper says observations are simply appended to the prompt. The orchestrator and prompt-building code was not in the truncated bundle.

observation_format.evidence_quote: After each action is taken, the agent receives a textual observation.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Signatures of Python functions corresponding to the allowed actions are provided in the prompt.
tool_call_format.note: Actions are logged as repl code (register_repl in base_agent.py). Locator refers to the Sec. 4.1 text.

tool_count.note: The paper describes roughly 6 action types (doc search, people search, send message, resolve person, end turn/session, reflection), but the plugin registry was not in the bundle.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The agent can perform a few types of actions.
edit_primitive.note: The action list contains no file editing.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Signatures of Python functions corresponding to the allowed actions are provided in the prompt.

protocol_standardization.note: Dependency files were not in the bundle.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: We consider an event-based reactive agent, which is triggered by user actions: upon getting a message from any or-ganization member, the agent follows ReAct-style prompting loop
loop_primitives.note: Also present in code: orchestrator_id event_driven_reactive (agent_config.py).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Our agent represents reflection as tool calls that return no value but re-main in the agent’s prompt at future timesteps.

multi_agent_topology.note: Other parties are simulated or human collaborators, not agents of the harness.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: hitl mode is set per user, so that some users can be simulated, while others can be through terminal
human_in_loop.note: 'HITL' here means humans playing collaborators, which is not a gate on the agent's actions.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: events, action, and observation are incrementally appended in the prompt in the order in which they occur

long_term_memory.note: The orchestrator and plugin code was not in the bundle.

self_verification.note: The LLM evaluator is used for benchmark scoring, not agent self-verification.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Turn and Session Completion: agent can mark the current turn or the entire session as completed.
termination_condition.note: Other caps may exist but were not visible in the evidence.

execution_isolation.note: Actions are simulated APIs; no execution backend was visible in the evidence.

tracing.evidence_quote: And compile it into AsyncCollabDatum for evaluation and replay.

target_domain.evidence_quote: PEOPLEJOIN is a benchmark for evaluating LM-mediated collaborative problem solving.
